implementation_notes: GameplayKit ships the pattern directly: GKQuadtree (2D) and GKOctree (3D) organize reference-type elements by point or region, with add(_:at:)/add(_:in:), remove(_:using:) and elements(at:)/elements(in:) queries; GKRTree provides the R-tree alternative and the documentation explains the tradeoff (quadtree faster for uniform or frequently moving objects, R-tree faster for region searches). GameplayKit is Apple-platforms-only, so a server-side or Linux Swift build falls back to a hand-written grid of cell arrays indexed by position - the classic structure is then justified. Moving an element means remove plus add again, so keep the GKQuadtreeNode returned by add for cheap removal.
pitfalls: Elements must be NSObject subclasses (reference semantics), so value-type entities need a wrapper before they can be indexed.
GKQuadtree is Apple-platforms-only; server-side Swift must fall back to a hand-written grid.
minimumCellSize bounds subdivision: too small subdivides excessively, too large degrades queries toward linear scans, and moving elements require remove plus add.
